Q1: Acrolein's hazard profile indicates known, significant dangers across multiple categories (Tier 1), including carcinogenicity, mutagenicity, or reproductive hazards (CMR), environmental hazards (ENV), inhalation hazards (IHL), oral hazards (ORL), dermal and eye hazards (SKN), and organ and systemic hazards (OGN). The only area with insufficient data to make a confident assessment is endocrine disruption (EDC), which is classified as Tier 4.
Q2: Acrolein is included on numerous prominent regulatory lists due to its recognized hazards. Notably, it is classified as an IARC Group 2A carcinogen and is listed under the Clean Water Act, Safe Drinking Water Act, and as a Hazardous Air Pollutant, reflecting significant environmental and public health concerns.
Q3: Acrolein is considered a very well-characterized chemical, supported by an extensive body of scientific literature with 28,000 references, far exceeding the typical chemical. Its molecular formula (C3H4O) is precisely defined, it is classified as a 'Small Molecule' rather than an ambiguously defined substance, and it is not designated as a UVCB, further confirming its clear characterization. Furthermore, only one out of its seven hazard classes lacks sufficient data for assessment.
